strengths: Every new test is behavioral: the parser, renderers and writers run for real on the make_toolbox demo archive, with no stubbed collaborators.

The parser refusals cover each documented case (missing, empty or name-only href, nested , unclosed at the end of a

, an

  • and the markup) with parametrized ids.

test_check_applied_reports_an_href_only_change_as_page_stale pins the key design decision: an href-only change is page_stale on every surface, not page_style_stale, so a generator sweep cannot publish unchecked targets; the paired guard test proves an unchanged href stays clean.
BAD_CANONICAL swaps its <a> for <code>, so the existing unsupported_tag expectation in test_arc_meta_api.py keeps a real unsupported tag now that <a> is supported.

The release-notes test globs docs/RELEASES/ and declares WALK_ROOTS accordingly, so selection reruns it on release-note edits, and its path strings carry the arc-straps anchor for plugin.json and README.md changes.
The skill contract's negative assertion ('no links' gone) is meaningful: it runs on whitespace-normalized text, where the old rule's 'no\n  links' line break would otherwise have hidden it.

text_with_links feeds only the comparison key, so an href-only edit reads as page_stale on the help page. Hover checks stay text-only because both sides of that comparison are xdoc or plain text without hrefs, so the checker and the writers stay consistent.
_para_problems surfaces the old silent loss of child elements inside a <para> (inner_html flattens them with itertext) as a named unsupported_para_markup problem with an actionable detail.
Href values are escaped for double-quoted attributes through one helper (_attr), used by both the Pro HTML and canonical renderers.
Pulling _run_canon out keeps to_canonical the inverse of parse: the link wraps the bold/italic markup, and the parser reads it back as the same runs.
Run.href defaults to None, so existing positional Run construction and _replace calls keep working unchanged.
The SKILL.md API row for check_canonical names `unsupported_para_markup`, which matches the new ProblemCode and the module docstrings in arc_meta_models.py and arc_meta_api.py.
The SKILL.md rule that a `<para>` holds plain text only matches the code: _para_problems covers the summary, the usage and each dialogReference.
The release table row, the plugin.json bump and the README sentence change together, and contract tests pin them so they cannot drift.
The plan records each decision with its rejected options and rationale, and gives the split-PR boundary (D10) with explicit version steps for PR A and PR B.

The parser refuses a nested , a missing or empty href, and an still open at

, , or the end of the markup, so an href cannot leak into the next block; the module docstring lists exactly these refusals.

Hover checks stay consistent: fields_of already flattens the summary to plain text and renders parameters as xdoc without hrefs, so text_with_links compares link-free strings on both sides of the rc check and only the page sees href changes.
plain_text and text_with_links share one _flatten helper, so plain_text's output is unchanged for every existing caller.

unsupported_para_markup closes a silent drop (inner_html flattens a <para> through itertext); the code ships in the models enum, the API check, the SKILL check_canonical row, the plugin README and the v0.7.0 notes together.
Hrefs round-trip safely: HTMLParser unescapes attribute values and _attr re-escapes &, <, > and double quotes for both the Pro <A HREF> and the canonical <a href>.

The parser refuses an unclosed `` at

, , and the end of the markup, so an href cannot leak into the next block, and test_an_unclosed_a_is_refused_at_the_end_of_its_block covers all three exits.

`_plain` switches to text_with_links, so an href-only change reads as page_stale instead of page_style_stale and a generator sweep cannot publish an unchecked link. A guard test pins that an unchanged href stays clean on both surfaces.
The writer tests run the real apply_page and apply_rc on a make_toolbox archive and then assert check_applied == []: behavioral end to end, with no mocks.

`_para_problems` reads the parsed `<para>` elements because inner_html has already dropped the children by the time `_rich_fields` sees the field. The check sits at the only layer that can see the markup.
`Run.href` defaults to None, so every positional Run(text, bold, italic) constructor and every _replace call keeps working, and link-free output stays byte-identical.

The release guards (manifest version in a release-notes row, manifest and marketplace descriptions equal) hold through both planned bumps and declare their WALK_ROOTS, so select_tests routes them correctly.

important.name: Authoring rule drops the relative-link warning while nothing checks relative hrefs
important.summary:
The old Format bullet explained that the "?" page renders from a temp copy, so relative links break. The new text (SKILL.md:140-143) allows any `` and removes that warning. The only code that reports relative hrefs, `link_relative` (plan D9, TASK-7), belongs to PR B and is still PENDING. At this head, arc-meta passes `docs/demo.html` or `../x.html` through to the page with no warning, and the skill no longer tells the author the link will be dead. The plan's own D9 rationale says a relative href "is dead on the '?' page". Also (skill_package): The Format bullet replaced 'no links (the "?" page is rendered from a temp copy, so relative links break ...)' with '`` passes through to the "?" page'. The reason the old rule gave still holds: Pro renders the page from %TEMP% (SKILL.md 179), so a relative href breaks. check_canonical accepts any non-empty href (arc_meta_format.py _open_link 93-100, SUPPORTED_TAGS now holds 'a'), and the link_relative check the plan assigns to arc-help-pages (plan D9) does not exist at this head. An author following the skill as merged writes , gets `clean` from check_canonical and check_applied, and publishes a dead link. Also (roast): The Format bullet says link targets and help pages 'belong to `arc-help-pages`', but this PR ships arc-straps 0.2.0 with only `arc-meta` (plugins/arc-straps/skills/ holds one skill). The plan makes arc-help-pages PR B (TASK-4 to TASK-9, PENDING), gated on a Pro click-test that 'can stop Section 3' (D10; TASK-4 notes). TASK-3.1 step 4 says 'No arc-help-pages mention anywhere: that is PR B', yet TASK-3 step 1 puts the name in this file. An agent that follows the bullet goes looking for a skill that is not installed, and if the Gate fails the pointer stays wrong for good. The contract test pins it too (tests/skills/test_arc_meta_skill_contract.py:152). It points at a skill that may never ship. Also (roast): The removed sentence explained that the "?" page is rendered from a temp copy, so relative links break. This PR adds `a` to SUPPORTED_TAGS (arc_meta_api.py:42), so `check_canonical` now reports `` as clean. The only check for relative hrefs, `link_relative` (D9), lives in PR B's check_links. In PR A nothing checks a relative href and nothing warns about it, so an author following the skill can ship a dead link to the "?" page with every check clean. The PR made links legal and removed the one sentence that said how to write them. Also (docs): SKILL.md:141-142 says link targets and help pages 'belong to `arc-help-pages`'. That skill does not exist at this head: plugins/arc-straps/skills/ holds only arc-meta, and plan TASK-4 to TASK-9 are PENDING. Plan D10 says the Gate can stop Section 3, and TASK-3.1 step 4 says there is 'No arc-help-pages mention anywhere: that is PR B'. arc-straps 0.2.0 therefore ships prose that sends an agent to a missing skill, possibly for good. The sentence is pinned by tests/skills/test_arc_meta_skill_contract.py:152. Also (skill_package): The Format bullet says 'link targets and help pages belong to `arc-help-pages`', but plugins/arc-straps/skills/ holds only arc-meta at 567b9c5; the skill arrives in a later PR (plan TASK-4 to TASK-9). Until then the pointer dangles, and a release cut in between ships arc-meta pointing at nothing. The plan itself says no arc-help-pages mention belongs in this PR's descriptions. Also (skill_package): SKILL.md 138-139 states 'The subset is `

`, ``, ``, `

    `/`
  • ` with one level of `
      ` inside an `
    • `', while the generator docstring (arc_meta_format.py 13-16) and SUPPORTED_TAGS (arc_meta_api.py 42) now put `` in the supported subset. The link sentence two lines later adds it back, so the bullet now gives the subset in two places that disagree. Also (roast): Before this PR, an `` or a bare `` collapsed to its text and check_canonical only reported unsupported_tag; the writers still applied. Now `_open_link` (arc_meta_format.py:93-100) raises, so check_canonical reports `unparseable` and apply_page, apply_rc and apply_toolbox's load_source refuse the field. The same applies to a nested or unclosed ``. arc_meta_format's docstring records the refusal, but the SKILL.md Format bullet, the plugin README sentence and the release-note line describe links only as passing through. A project with an old named anchor learns about this when its apply stops.

minor.name: Plan records an absolute machine path into a consuming project
minor.summary:
`source_document` (ActionPlan.json:4, rendered as PIP.md:6 **Spec:**) is `E:/automation/toolboxes/floodplain_development/docs/...`. That is a local absolute path into another repository, so nobody else can open it from this repo, and it names a consuming project in a tracked file. `deferred_to_future_plans` (ActionPlan.json:1720) also names that project. Most other plans cite a repo-relative spec or an issue URL (0002 to 0011).

Also (docs): Plans in docs/plans run 0001 to 0011, and this plan is 1011. harness_lib.plan_doc.next_plan_id (plan_doc.py:48-51) returns the highest four-digit prefix plus one, so every later plan will be numbered from 1012, leaving a gap of 1000. The id looks like a typo for 0012, or like a number carried over from the consuming project.

Also (roast): `source_document` is 'E:/automation/toolboxes/floodplain_development/docs/...', a local absolute path into another repository, and the notes and deferred topics name the consuming project. The PIP renders the path again at line 6. CLAUDE.md's literal ban covers only plugins/, but tracked docs that carry machine paths go against the repository's rule that logged data never carries local paths. Plan 0001 is the only precedent.
fix: Point `source_document` at a repo-independent reference: an issue URL, or a copy of the spec committed under docs/superpowers/specs/. Change it through the plan driver and re-render the PIP. Write the deferred topic generically ('migrate the consuming project to arc-straps').
Renumber to 0012 before merge: rename both files and docs/plans/1011/ (local, gitignored), then update `plan_id`, `documentation` and the 'docs/plans/1011/tests' text in each action, and re-render.
Or keep 1011 on purpose and say why in the PR description.

Record the spec as a project-neutral reference (for example 'consuming project: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-09-toolbox-help-links-design.md') through the plan driver and re-render; or accept this as plan-tooling convention and note it.

Archive the planned test files somewhere tracked, or force-add them on PR B's branch, so the pending tasks can be executed from main.

minor.name: Open link leaks across an implicitly closed block
minor.summary:
The docstring at arc_meta_format.py:102-103 says the open-link refusal stops an href leaking into the next block, and the module docstring (lines 21-22) says an still open where its paragraph or list item ends raises ValueError. The check only runs on explicit end tags (handle_endtag, lines 170-171). HTMLParser does not synthesize end tags, so in `
  • a
  • b
` or `

one

two

` the second
  • /

    start opens a new block with self._href still set. Its text becomes a link run with href x, and the later closes it cleanly, so nothing is refused. Also (runtime): _open_link (arc_meta_format.py:97-100) refuses only a falsy href. `href=" "` passes and renders as , an href with surrounding spaces is kept as written, and the docstring's 'missing or empty href' refusal does not cover either case. Also, `` or ` ` produces no run, because handle_data drops whitespace-only text. The authored link then disappears from every surface without the ValueError the module docstring promises for malformed links.
fix: In handle_starttag, call self._refuse_open_link(f"<{tag}>") before handling tag in ("p", "para", "li", "ul"), so a block that opens while a link is still open is refused the same way an explicit end tag is.

Strip the href before the check (`href = (dict(attrs).get("href") or "").strip()`; refuse when empty, store the stripped value). Track whether the open link received a text run, and raise ValueError(" without text") at when it did not.

....

Or keep the behavior and update the fields_of and rc_text docstrings in arc_meta_canonical.py to say a link also selects xdoc, even though xdoc keeps only the link text.
